description: TLS 1.2 renegotiation allows clients to change servername unilaterally to bypass client certificate authentication
overview: A client certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS lets a client change the `servername` during TLS 1.2 renegotiation to reach endpoints it was not authorized for. On a server that applies different client-certificate policies per hostname, for example stricter admin-only client-cert auth on one host and ordinary client-cert auth on another, a client that authenticates for a permitted host can renegotiate the TLS 1.2 connection under a different `servername` and carry its existing authentication to the protected host, bypassing the stricter policy. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
